source.title: Large Language Model Unlearning via Embedding-Corrupted Prompts
source.authors: Chris Liu; Yaxuan Wang; Jeffrey Flanigan; Yang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a different unlearning approach—input-embedding corruption with an unchanged model—and tests whether targeted accuracy remains near chance and whether a linear probe can recover answers from output logits.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test fine-tuning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery attacks on gradient-ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU-unlearned models. RMU and other baselines' unlearning scores are not recovery-attack results and are not included. Classifier error rates and illustrative generations are not target-knowledge recovery measurements. Probe outcomes are described in text but shown only in a figure.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes ECO, an inference-time guardrail: a prompt classifier plus embedding corruption, with weights unchanged. Its own results bear on version A. They report near-chance WMDP and MMLU-subset forget accuracy with unchanged MMLU, and a linear probe on output logits that stays at chance. It also reports RMU checkpoints, an original-source method, failing on chemistry and damaging related retain subjects. It runs no fine-tuning, ablation or quantization recovery attacks. Prompt-attack robustness is measured only as classifier error rates.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that classifier-gated embedding-corrupted prompts impose an unlearned state on an intact LLM. This state approximates a retained model across TOFU, WMDP/MMLU and copyright tasks, with near-zero utility loss, scaling to 100 models up to 236B. Logit probes stay at chance. They acknowledge that open-weight access or adversarial attacks on the classifier can bypass it.
record.recipe_differences: ECO keeps the underlying LLM weights unchanged and uses a prompt classifier plus learned embedding corruption during inference; it is not gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, or RMU unlearning.
record.method_sensitivity: For WMDP, one corruption strength is optimized on Zephyr-7B using synthetic questions and reused across other models. Appendix D.2 reports that corruption strength tuning matters for TOFU, and classifier thresholding choices change false-positive and false-negative rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompt-classifier false-negative rates under rephrased, adversarial and jailbreak-like prompts. The original TOFU classifier misses 7.52% of jailbreak-prefixed prompts; the WMDP classifier after augmentation misses 3.5%. Missed prompts would reach the uncorrupted model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Guardrail-style unlearning is bypassed by jailbreak prompts at a rate equal to the classifier's false-negative rate.

record.problems: The central probe results are presented in a figure without exact values in the text. The paper states experiments were repeated at least three times and averaged but does not provide error bars or statistical-significance results for every experiment. Results concern ECO, not recovery attacks on conventional weight-unlearning methods.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the row limit. Other task results, large model sweeps, and additional copyrighted-content tables were not extracted because they do not report the recovery attacks named in the claim.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning, activation ablation, quantization or weight-access attacks on ECO. The authors concede open-weight access bypasses the classifier. Prompting attacks are measured only as classifier FNR/FPR, not as recovered accuracy.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack on any method.
No activation-direction ablation or internal analysis of any weight-unlearned model.
No measurement of knowledge recovered by rephrasing, jailbreaks or other languages. Only classifier error rates under such prompts are reported.
ECO's robustness to the B–E attacks is not tested. Only an output-logit probe and classifier robustness to OOD prompts are reported.

missing.what: RMU baseline results. WMDP: Zephyr 29.7/47.1/28.1, MMLU 57.5; Yi-34B 31.0/54.7/27.9; Mixtral 32.0/52.7/31.4. MMLU subsets: forget ~27; econometrics 41.2, jurisprudence 37.0, math 29.2.

ECO WMDP and MMLU-subset results across 78 general and 22 specialized models (forget accuracy 21.5–27.7 on WMDP). Economics forget accuracy stays at 35.8 for several models because predictions are biased toward answer D.
TOFU forget quality depends on the corruption function and strength. For example, random-noise Top-k on Llama forget-10% gives 0.0000 vs zero-out 0.98.
Classifier FNR/FPR under out-of-distribution and jailbreak prompts.

record.verdict_notes: ECO is a guardrail rather than weight-level unlearning. Its support for A holds only in a gray-box API setting and by design leaves the knowledge in the weights, which is consistent with the shallow-unlearning concern rather than refuting it. Retain scores are unchanged because the classifier routes prompts, not because knowledge was selectively removed.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests ECO, not the listed conventional unlearning methods; its probe evaluation is a linear probe on output logits, not the fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks named in the claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation; the paper's input-corruption interpretation analysis does not test restoration by an internal edit.
No quantization attack on unlearned weights.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language-switching, or in-context recovery attack on unlearned weights.
ECO is evaluated with a linear probe, but the paper does not test its resistance to the fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, or prompting attacks listed in the claim.

tranche.reason: ECO is a different method (classifier plus embedding corruption) aimed at the same question, measured by WMDP and MMLU accuracy. It also evaluates the released RMU checkpoints.

source_check.notes: ECO keeps MMLU identical by construction, and σ was tuned only on Zephyr-7B. No attack on the classifier was run; probes (figure-only) cover models up to 47B. WMDP RMU numbers come from the released cais checkpoints (App. C.4). The authors link the chemistry retention to the 'available data for unlearning'.

statements.correction: Zephyr-7B: Bio 64.2→24.7, Chem 48.3→26.5, Cyber 43.1→24.4. Bio: Yi-34B-Chat 76.2→25.9; Mixtral-8x7B 71.6→25.0; Mixtral-8x22B (141B) 77.3→26.7; DeepSeek-V2-Chat (236B) 76.5→23.2. Full MMLU and Table 2 retain subjects are unchanged. Probe at chance (Figure 3, figure-only). σ was tuned on Zephyr-7B only. Scale: up to 236B in Table 1; 100 LLMs (0.5B–236B) in the appendix.
statements.problem: The ECO numbers and conditions are right. But the why line says 'up to 141B', and Table 1 also has DeepSeek-V2-Chat (236B). The paper covers 100 LLMs from 0.5B to 236B.

statements.correction: ECO edits no weights; it is weak unlearning in output space (Sec. 2.1–2.2). Appendix B: unlearning holds only with API access; an open-weight adversary could circumvent it by bypassing the classifier. Not tested. Verdict l2 is limits_scope. r1: Zephyr Bio 64.2→24.7; r15: DeepSeek-V2 Cyber 48.9→23.8.
statements.problem: The facts are right (weights unchanged; Appendix B). But Appendix B says an adversary 'could circumvent', and no bypass was tested. This study's verdict for the API-only condition is limits_scope, not challenges. Cited rows r1 and r15 show forgetting near chance, not recovery.

statements.correction: Models above 100B in this study: Mixtral-8x22B (141B) and DeepSeek-V2-Chat (236B) in Table 1; falcon-180B-chat and Qwen1.5-110B-Chat in Tables 20–22. None has a recovery attack. The only recovery attempt is a logit linear probe on Zephyr-7B, Yi-34B-Chat and Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (47B).
statements.problem: It says Mixtral-8x22B is the only model above 100B. Table 1 also has DeepSeek-V2-Chat (236B, r13–r15). The appendix WMDP tables add falcon-180B-chat and Qwen1.5-110B-Chat. The main point holds: no model above 100B is attacked.
